note: Switchable patches of GOWA.SELF 1.12 (ppu, data and spu edits). Each is off unless switched on ([patches] <id> = on in ascension-r.ini, --set patches.<id>=on, or GOWA_PATCH_<ID>=1), or, with "default": true, on unless switched off (= off, =0). `gowa.py lift` lifts every ppu edit in both forms behind the patch's guard (ppu_lifter --insn-patches), every spu edit the same way in its job module (spu_lifter --insn-patches), and writes recompiled/gowa_title_patches.h; patches.cpp writes the data edits and sets the guard once the ELF is in guest memory, before the title runs. Every orig is checked against the ELF at the lift, and the data again in guest memory: a patch for another build of the title is refused. The sites were found with RPCS3's patch list for this build as a map, and each one read back from this ELF (docs/notes/2026-11-01-title-patches.md). `gowa.py patches` lists them and checks them against the ELF.

patches.name: Disable MLAA
patches.note: The title's SPU anti-aliasing: five taskset tasks a frame over a copy of the frame. This port never shows their output (its frame stays on the GPU), so they only cost time. The word at 0x83D004 is the title's own MLAA switch, read in 18 places from its init to every frame (func_0041C344 arms the MLAA counter with it); at 0 the title takes its own paths without MLAA.

ppu.note: func_003973D0: bl 0x397408, the 64-bit entry it builds with r4 = 4
func_003973D0: bl 0x397408, the entry with r4 = 6 (the one with r4 = 5, between them, stays)

data.note: the low byte of the MLAA word 0x83D004: 1 -> 0

patches.name: Disable Depth of Field
patches.note: Reads the effect's enable as 0 in its update. The same code as Motion Blur's: the field at +0x20 of the effect's object, read before cmpwi r5,0.

patches.name: Disable Motion Blur
patches.note: Reads the effect's enable as 0 in its update, as Depth of Field's.

patches.name: Disable Mesh Trimming
patches.note: In EDGE's SPU geometry code, the same instruction of both EDGE job modules. RPCS3's note: it lets the title draw correctly above the PS3's resolutions, and keeps the signed-area, back-face and later culling stages. For drawing above 720p, not for speed: it can only add geometry. The modules' bytes in guest memory stay as they are; the lifted code takes the replacement (an SPU interpreted there would not).

spu.note: the same in the other EDGE module, a second build of it the first levels do not run and the Grotto does. Only a pointer reaches the function, 0xE35C (the same code as the first module's 0xD92C): its lift ended at 0xB90C until the entries of issue #7's missed code moved it out to 0xF1C4 (2026-11-12), and the Grotto's jobs ran it interpreted, unpatched. Optional: a lift that does not reach it reports it

patches.name: Disable Shadows
patches.note: Not one of RPCS3's. The title's dynamic shadows are its fxNewShadows effect (RTTI 12fxNewShadows, vtable 0x6A5940; per-frame update func_00376748, slot 2). Its update reads the effect's enable at +0x20, as Depth of Field's and Motion Blur's do (the same base: bl 0x3B69B8 on this+16 just before); when it is 0 the title clears the renderer's shadow parameter block (memset 0x982F08, 120 bytes) instead of copying the effect's parameters into it. The edit makes that read 0 (docs/notes/2026-11-03-disable-shadows.md). Skipping the whole update instead (its vtable slot pointed at a bare blr) left no shadow map either, but the fight then drew giant copies of Megaera's wings where the sky is.

patches.name: Unlock FPS (experimental)
patches.note: Lets the title run past 60 frames a second at its own speed (docs/notes/2026-11-23-unlock-fps.md). It steps its world by the real time of each frame, counted in periods of 1/rate (rate 59.94, the global 0x83B45C, set once by func_002D01E8): func_002D0258 clamps that count to 1-4 periods, so a frame under 16.7 ms still moved it by 16.7 ms, and above 60 fps it ran fast. With the rate 1000 a period is 1 ms: the clamp's floor is 1 ms, and its ceiling stays 66.7 ms. The rate global keeps 59.94 for its other readers (gameplay code that scales by it), while the time count, the frame sync and the video player read 1000.0. RPCS3's "Unlock FPS" v2.0 for 1.04 as the map (its 1.12 v1.0, which handed 1000 to every reader, was taken out of its list); each site read back from this ELF. Beyond it: func_002D0258's two fixed steps, one period when 0x9424D8 forces it and mode 4's two, are kept at 16.7 and 33.4 ms (their constants are that function's alone). The frame clock (main.cpp) then lets flips come sooner than a vblank period: [display] fps_limit, 120 by default.

ppu.note: func_002D01E8, the rate set (once, at init): stfs f1,0xb45c(r4) -> nop, so the global keeps the data edit's 59.94
func_002CA76C, the time count: lfs f2,0xb45c(r3) -> lfs f2,0x948c(r3), the TOC word 0x83948C, 1000.0
func_002D0258, the frame sync: lfs f1,0xb45c(r5) -> 1000.0
func_002D0258: its second read of the rate, lfs f1,0xb45c(r3) -> 1000.0
func_003F5748, the video player: lfs f31,0xb45c(r4) -> 1000.0, so a video keeps its speed

data.note: the rate table's 59.94 -> 1000.0: the rate set gives 1 ms periods (int rate 1000)
func_002D0258's ceiling 400 (4 periods, 66.7 ms) -> 6667 (66.67 ms of 1 ms periods): the same longest step
func_002D0258's 1.0, the one period 0x9424D8 forces -> 16.6834 (1000/59.94): still 16.7 ms
the rate global: 59.94 from the start, as the rate set would have made it (its store is a nop now)
checked only: the TOC word the four loads read, 0x447A0000, a link-time constant that is 1000.0 as a float
